source.title: Steering CLIP's vision transformer with sparse autoencoders
source.authors: Sonia Joseph; Praneet Suresh; E. Gol'dfarb; Lorenz Hufe; Yossi Gandelsman; Robert Graham; D. Bzdok; W. Samek; Blake Richards

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary material are present. Some tables are flattened in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports results about CLIP neuron steering and polysemanticity, but does not measure any of the listed versions’ specified claims: neuron-pole job shares, the Inception example, attribution-graph explanations, or held-out explanation scores.
record.gate_note: The neuron-versus-SAE steering comparison and the statement about maximally activating images are relevant to the broader question of neurons as analysis units, but do not measure the outcomes named by any claim version. The paper also reports task-specific ablations and typographic-attack results; these evaluate disentanglement and defense performance, not the listed claims.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs on CLIP-ViT-B-32 and compares SAE-feature with neuron steering and ablation. It reports no share of neurons with one or two jobs, no InceptionV1 cat/car analysis, no attribution graphs, and no held-out explanation scoring. Its neuron results (steering coverage, qualitative top-image polysemanticity) measure related but different constructs, so they belong under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also stress sparsity differences between vision and language SAEs (spatial-token L0 3-14x GPT-2's), and that 10-15% of features in deeper layers are steerable. They report state-of-the-art typographic-attack defense on PAINT, and top results when combined with Defense-Prefix.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains sparse autoencoders on CLIP vision-transformer activations and evaluates steering and targeted feature suppression; it does not use the neuron-pole audit or explanation-testing procedure described in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that steerable-feature prevalence is analyzed using a threshold of γ = 0.10, and that the neuron-versus-feature coverage comparison is at layer 11 using a 5,000-concept vocabulary.

fits_no_version.finding: At layer 11 of CLIP-ViT-B-32, residual-stream neuron steering reached about 1% of 5,000 concepts (~50), versus ~11% (~550) for SAE features. The paper also says steerable neuron and feature proportions are similar (10-15%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In CLIP's vision transformer, SAE features give far wider steering concept coverage than residual-stream neurons, mainly through greater dimensionality.

fits_no_version.finding: Base-network neurons selected for task attributes look polysemantic in their top activating images, while SAE features show the attribute. This is qualitative only (Figures 2 and 10).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-selected CLIP residual neurons appear polysemantic on visual inspection of top activating images.

record.peer_reviewed: Accepted to the CVPR 2025 Workshop on Mechanistic Interpretability for Vision (MIV)
record.problems: The neuron-versus-feature steering comparison uses a sample of 25% of features and neurons, and the concept vocabulary contains 5,000 terms. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the comparison. The paper's qualitative neuron interpretation does not provide a systematic count of interpretable or polysemantic neurons.
record.rows_left_out: The paper's targeted CelebA and Waterbirds ablations and typographic-attack benchmark results were left out because they measure task performance and defense effectiveness, not the outcomes named by the claim versions. Other SAE sparsity and training metrics likewise do not measure neuron-job shares or explanation fidelity.

untested.parts: Untested in full: no Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or job-share counts.
Untested in full: no language-model job shares across dense or MoE models or scale.
Untested in full: no InceptionV1 cat/car neuron, pose, or recursive-generalization analysis.
Untested in full: no interpretable-neuron shares by tool or architecture.
Untested in full: no attribution graphs or replacement-model reconstruction error.
Untested in full: no test of activating-example explanations against firing prediction.
Untested in full: no simulation-based explanation scoring.

record.verdict_notes: The neurons studied are residual-stream dimensions of CLIP-ViT-B-32, not MLP neuron poles. This makes even a loose link to V1, V2 or V4 weak. There are no uncertainty estimates. The neuron-ablation control in Table 1 barely changes accuracy, but that measures task disentanglement, not neuron interpretability.

versions.untested_parts: Does not audit Qwen3-32B neuron poles or report counts of poles with one job, two jobs, or unexplained jobs.
Studies CLIP-ViT-B-32, a vision model; it does not measure neuron-job shares across language models, dense and MoE architectures, or model scales.
Does not analyze InceptionV1's cat-and-car neuron, pose, or recursive generalization.
Does not estimate interpretable-neuron shares in InceptionV1-sized vision models or test whether tools or architecture change those shares.
Compares neuron and SAE-feature steering, not attribution graphs, behavioral explanations, replacement models, or reconstruction error.
Does not test explanations against held-out activations or measure whether explanations predict where neurons fire.
Does not score neuron explanations by simulated activations on new text.

rows.subject: CLIP-ViT-B-32
rows.operation_detail: Compared neuron-level steering with SAE-feature steering for concept-space coverage.
rows.value: Neuron steering accessed only 1% of concepts (about 50 concepts).
rows.note: The paper compares steering coverage, not the ability of neurons to explain behavior using attribution graphs.
rows.check: Steering concept coverage of residual-stream neurons is not a neuron job-share or explanation-fidelity measure. Note: these are residual-stream basis directions, not MLP neurons.

rows.subject: CLIP-ViT-B-32
rows.operation_detail: Compared neuron-level steering with SAE-feature steering for concept-space coverage.
rows.value: Feature steering accessed approximately 11% of concepts (about 550 concepts).
rows.note: The reported coverage is more than 10 times that of neuron steering in this comparison.
rows.check: This is the study's own method (SAE features) set against neurons. It is a method-comparison row and does not measure neurons' interpretability shares.

rows.subject: CLIP-ViT-B-32
rows.operation_detail: Examined maximally activating images for selected base-model neurons.
rows.value: The authors describe base-model neurons as highly polysemantic.
rows.note: The authors contrast these images with SAE features that show task-relevant attributes; they do not quantify neuron job counts.
rows.check: A qualitative label for neurons selected by task-attribute activation differences (Fτl*). It is a selected handful, not an audit sample, and gives no count.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
